questions.problem: Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ Find the likelihood function of the sample $2.1,\,5.0,\,4.2,\,1.4.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}\theta {e}^{-\theta {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-\theta \sum {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-S\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$ 

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =2.1+5.0+4.2+1.4 \\  & =12.7\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\theta }^{4}\,{e}^{-12.7\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{6}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,1),$  where $\theta $ is an unknown mean. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{6},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{6}{x}_{i}=5.2,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{6}{x}_{i}^{2}=22.6.
$$

Given that the likelihood function of the sample is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{8{\pi }^{3}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$

*Hint: The probability density function for a normal random variable with mean $\theta $ and variance $1$ is given by* 

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=6$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=5.2,$ $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}=22.6,$ and $n=6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-6/2}\,{e}^{-(22.6-2(5.2)\theta +6{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8{\pi }^{3}}\,{e}^{\,-11.3\,+\,5.2\theta \,-\,3{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-11.3+5.2\theta -3{\theta }^{2}.
$$

Given that the likelihood function of the sample is

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{256{\pi }^{8}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$

*Hint: The probability density function for a normal random variable with mean $\theta $ and variance $1$ is given by*

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=16$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=-13.2,$ $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}=33.2,$ and $n=16.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-16/2}\,{e}^{-(33.2-2(-13.2)\theta +16{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{256{\pi }^{8}}\,{e}^{\,-16.6\,-\,13.2\theta \,-\,8{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-16.6-13.2\theta -8{\theta }^{2}.

$$
L(\theta )=\frac{1}{8{\pi }^{3}}\,{e}^{\,g(\theta )},
$$

what is the expression for $g(\theta )?$

Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=6$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{x-\theta }{\sigma })}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-\sum ({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(\sum {x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta \sum {x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =(2\pi )^{-n/2}\,{e}^{-(C-2S\theta +n{\theta }^{2})/2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $C={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}.$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =1.7+2.3+2.2+1.1+1.9+1.8 \\  & =11 \\ C & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =(1.7)^{2}+(2.3)^{2}+(2.2)^{2}+(1.1)^{2}+(1.9)^{2}+(1.8)^{2} \\  & =21.08\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =(2\pi )^{-6/2}\,{e}^{-(21.08-2(11)\theta +6{\theta }^{2})/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8{\pi }^{3}}\,{e}^{\,-10.54\,+\,11\theta \,-\,3{\theta }^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
g(\theta )=-10.54+11\theta -3{\theta }^{2}.
$$
